newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania ARD tries to amend foreign investment law.
newsitem.headline: Romania ARD tries to amend foreign investment law.

text.p: Romania's main foreign investment promoter said on Wednesday it had worked out amendments to the country's foreign investment law to bring it in line with Western standards.
The draft is aimed at simplifying investment procedures and granting more incentives to foreign investors.

"The current legislation should be updated and harmonised with the legislation of European Union countries considering the perspective of Romania's integration into the EU and Euro-Atlantic structures," said a statement from the Romanian Development Agency (ARD).
The draft shows existing facilities, including automatic exemption from customs duties, should go hand in hand with additional ones, promoted by the Romanian government.
Legislation should allow the government to grant special facilities according to the worth, quality and importance of each foreign investment project, the statement said.
Foreign capital inflows are crucial for the implementation of a tough economic reform package which Romania's new government launched last month.

The new facilities envisaged by the ARD -- to benefit companies with a capital of minimum $10 million -- include profit tax breaks, extension of customs duties holidays, as well as free acquisition of land and of production spaces.
Under the present rules companies must invest a minimum $50 million to benefit from such facilities.
The centrist government coalition, which came to power after last November's elections replacing leftists, has pledged to support the rise in foreign investment.
Earlier this month, Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said over the next two months his government would work out or revise around 80 laws to draw in badly-needed foreign investments.

Direct foreign investment in seven years since Romania shed communism in 1989 stood at $2.25 billion early in March, an amount local economists say Romania now needs every year to be able to proceed with its reforms.
The amendments are welcome "in the new political context when growing foreign companies' interest in investing in Romania can be noted," the statement said.
